title: hybrid-prefetch-selector-and-kv-fragmentation-fixer-for-llama-mistral-qwen
author: Priya Shah
description:
Background and motivation: We observed a recurring tail-latency regression for a subset of MQA/GQA model configurations (notably Llama-2 MQA variants and some Mistral GQA workloads) under mixed-length traffic. Root cause analysis showed two compounding issues: 1) kernel routing oscillation between planar and interleaved code paths when head counts and active sequence lengths straddle optimization boundaries, and 2) KV cache fragmentation where frequent short-lived requests left many small slab allocations that reduced contiguous memory locality and increased prefetch overhead.

This PR introduces two coordinated runtime changes to address the problems without breaking existing behavior: a) Hybrid Prefetch Selector: a lightweight per-model selector that chooses between eager planar prefetch, conservative interleaved prefetch, or a hybrid selective prefetch based on an online histogram of recent prefix lengths and head-count hints. The selector is implemented as a small stateful policy that runs in the kernel router path and is feature-gated (ff.hybrid_prefetch_selector) so it can be gradually enabled per-model. b) KV Fragmentation Coalescer: a background compaction step in the KV slab allocator that coalesces adjacent small allocations into larger contiguous slabs when utilization and fragmentation thresholds are met. The coalescer is run opportunistically during low-load scheduling windows to avoid interference with latency-critical requests.

Key changes and rationale: - runtime/kernel_router.cpp: add HybridPrefetchSelector with a history window and decay-weighted histogram; expose per-model kernel hints used by dispatch. The selector avoids deterministic flips by adding hysteresis thresholds. - runtime/kv/slab_allocator.cpp: implement fragmentation scanner and coalescer, with a tunable heuristic for max coalesce bytes and time budget. - runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cpp: small adjustment to shortburst cutoff to cooperate with the new prefetch strategy (reduces false-positive eager prefetches for sub-16-token bursts). - api/model_hints.yaml: add documented hint options and default values for known GQA/MQA quirks. - tests/perf/bench_kv_coalesce.sh and tests/perf/bench_prefetch_selector.py: microbench harnesses used during development, plus end-to-end latency/throughput comparisons.

Performance summary (representative benchmarks): - Llama-2-70B (MQA) mixed-length chat workload: +12% throughput at 99th percentile SLA load, p95 latency -9ms (-11%). - Mistral-8G (GQA-like shaping): p95 -6ms (-8%), throughput +7% under 8-32 token dominated traffic. - Qwen-14B (edge cases with odd head counts): p95 -5ms, tail improvements most visible under small-batch/high-concurrency. - Average GPU memory overhead: +1.2% for KV coalescer metadata while running; coalescer idle during steady-state once fragmentation reduced.

Compatibility and rollout: - Feature gated behind ff.hybrid_prefetch_selector and ff.kv_coalescer. Default: off for existing customers; enabled by default in canary clusters for the next two weeks. - Backwards compatible kernel routing fallbacks preserved; we add extra logging under runtime.debug.prefetch to aid rollout monitoring.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for selector hysteresis and allocator coalescing logic - [x] Microbench harnesses committed - [x] Internal canary runs (3 regions) - [x] SLO smoke test for p50/p95/p99 on known workloads - [x] Security review for allocator changes (no changes to auth surface)

Release notes: Adds a new runtime optimization that reduces KV cache fragmentation and smooths kernel routing for mixed-length MQA/GQA workloads; opt-in via runtime feature flags.

References: ENG-8274 (investigation), ENG-8321 (scheduler follow-up), SUP-4123 (customer-reported tail incidents).

review_conversation: Ethan Lee: Can you explain why hysteresis is fixed instead of adaptive? We saw oscillation in an earlier attempt.

Priya Shah: Hysteresis is tuned using decay-weighted histograms; adaptive hysteresis was considered but added complexity and a small risk of overfitting. We can add telemetry if we see oscillation in canary.
Marta Alvarez: The coalescer might introduce latency spikes if it runs during a short high-load window. Can we enforce a CPU/time budget?
Priya Shah: Yes; coalescer has a time_budget_ms and only runs when scheduler detects a quiet slot. Added a guard in slab_allocator to abort compaction if scheduler load rises.
David Chen: CI flake on allocator unit test (race) — please fix with proper locking.
Priya Shah: Fixed in commit 0b2c4f8, added a comment and reduced shared state. Reran CI.
Ethan Lee: Approving after verifying perf numbers in canary. Minimal memory overhead and no regressions on non-targeted models.
Marta Alvarez: Approved. Requested we gate enablement per-model in the rollout plan (added to canary doc).
release_notes: Adds hybrid prefetch selector and KV fragmentation coalescer to reduce tail latency for MQA/GQA workloads; feature-flagged rollout. See api/model_hints.yaml for per-model tuning.
